issues.title: PowerShell parameter binder intercepts `-v` flag, breaking `snapshot -v 0`

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s news snapshot -v 0 --stdout
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Snapshot with viewport 0 captured and printed to stdout.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: CLI help text followed by: Error: Unknown command: 'snapshot-0'. Did you mean: 'snapshot'?
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: PowerShell's common parameter binder matches `-v` to `-Verbose` and consumes it before it reaches the `$RemainingArgs` array. The CLI binary then sees `snapshot 0` as two positional arguments and concatenates them into the subcommand `snapshot-0`, which doesn't exist.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1 line 16-20: param() block does not use CmdletBinding attribute but PowerShell still applies common parameters to script files. The SafeArgs loop at lines 442-446 double-quotes arguments but cannot recover arguments already consumed by PowerShell's binder.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add explicit `[CmdletBinding()]` with `-v` aliased away, or rename the script to avoid PowerShell parameter binding entirely
- Alternatively, remove the recommendation to use `./b4w.ps1` in the task instructions and always use `./b4w.sh` on non-Windows, which doesn't have this problem
- The `--` passthrough (documented in SKILL.md and b4w.ps1 help) should be fixed — it also failed with ambiguous parameter error
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Misleading error message when `-v` flag is consumed by PowerShell

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s news snapshot -v 0 --stdout
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A clear error indicating that the flag was not recognized, or a hint about PowerShell parameter binding.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Error: Unknown command: 'snapshot-0'. Did you mean: 'snapshot'? — the full help text is printed, and the error provides no hint that PowerShell intercepted the flag.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The CLI binary's argument parser receives `snapshot` followed by `0` (because `-v` was consumed) and tries to resolve `snapshot 0` as a subcommand named `snapshot-0`, which doesn't exist. The error message reflects the parser's best guess but is misleading because the user never typed `snapshot-0`.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — the command dispatcher that concatenates command tokens with hyphens to resolve subcommands (e.g., snapshot + grep → snapshot-grep).
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add detection: if a flag-like token (single-char prefixed with `-`) would have resolved the command, suggest that the flag may have been consumed by the shell/wrapper
- In b4w.ps1, detect when common parameters like `-Verbose` are passed and warn the user before the binary runs
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Session management workflow is discoverable but `-s` is a positional constraint

sections.body: Try `./b4w.ps1 snapshot -s news -v 0` (swapping `-s` position).
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The `-s` flag should work in any position before the command.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Not tested, but the help syntax `browser4-cli -s <session> <command> [args]` strongly implies `-s` must precede the command. A user accustomed to GNU-style argument parsing might place it anywhere and get confusing errors.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The CLI uses a positional argument parser where `-s` must appear before the subcommand. This is documented but not enforced with a helpful error when violated.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — argument parsing logic that processes global flags before subcommand dispatch.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Accept `-s <name>` in any position relative to the subcommand (more forgiving parsing)
- If the current constraint is intentional, add a clear error message when `-s` appears after the subcommand: 'The -s flag must be placed before the command. Try: browser4-cli -s news snapshot'
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `b4w.sh` emits noisy pwsh recommendation on every invocation

sections.body: Run any command via ./b4w.sh on Linux.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Clean output without platform-inappropriate warnings.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Every command prints: 'It is strongly recommended to launch `pwsh` and run the .ps1 commands directly within the `pwsh` terminal.' This is irrelevant on Linux where bash is the native shell.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The b4w.sh wrapper unconditionally prints this recommendation, likely as a development-time reminder that wasn't conditioned on the platform.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.sh: the echo/pwsh recommendation line near the top of the script.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Only print the pwsh recommendation when the detected shell environment could benefit from it (i.e., suppress it when pwsh is not installed or on Linux/macOS)
- Or gate it behind a `--verbose` flag or environment variable
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `snapshot -v 0 --stdout` produces excessively large output that overwhelms the terminal

sections.body: ./b4w.sh -s news snapshot -v 0 --stdout on a page with many elements.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Manageable output or a clear warning about expected size.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Output was 63.9KB for Hacker News and 36.8KB for Wikipedia. The output was so large it was persisted to a file instead of displayed inline. A first-time user would be overwhelmed.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: `--stdout` dumps the entire accessibility tree for the viewport chunk, which can be very large for content-rich pages. The SKILL.md warns about snapshot file size ('Don't cat snapshot files — they can exceed 256KB') but does not warn about `--stdout` behavior.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a note in SKILL.md explicitly warning that `--stdout` can produce very large output, recommending `snapshot grep` for targeted searches or `-i` for interactive elements only
- Consider adding a `--max-lines` flag to truncate `--stdout` output
- Add a tip after large `--stdout` output suggesting `snapshot grep` as an alternative
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Pre-existing '(default)' session appears without user action

sections.body: Run `./b4w.sh list` after first opening named sessions.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Only explicitly-created named sessions appear, or the default session's origin is explained.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: A '(default)' session appeared in the list with a UUID session ID, created earlier. A new user might be confused about where this session came from and whether it's safe to close.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Browser4 backend creates a default session when first started (e.g., by a previous `goto` without `-s`). The session persists until explicitly closed. New users have no context about this lifecycle.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a brief explanation in the `list` output or help text that '(default)' is the unnamed session created automatically when no `-s` flag is provided
- Consider adding a first-run message: 'No session specified — using (default). Use -s <name> for named sessions.'
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `goto` output doesn't clearly indicate a redirect occurred

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s research goto "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Browser_automation"
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Clear indication that the URL was redirected to a different page.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The output shows the final URL (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headless_browser) and title (Headless browser - Wikipedia) but doesn't mention that a redirect occurred from the requested URL.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The `goto` command reports the final page state after navigation, including any redirects, without distinguishing between direct loads and redirects. The user might think they navigated to the wrong page.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- When the final URL differs from the requested URL, include a note like '(redirected from <original URL>)' in the output
- Or include the original requested URL alongside the final URL in the page summary
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
